units.title: Energy and Chemical Reactions
units.intro: Energy is conserved. In chemistry we track heat. Breaking bonds *takes* energy (endothermic). Making bonds *releases* energy (exothermic). The sign of the whole reaction is which side wins.

5.1.1 Law of Conservation of Energy
body: All matter possesses energy in one form or another.
The different forms of kinetic energy include thermal energy and electrical energy.
The different forms of potential energy include chemical energy and gravitational energy.
The most common form of energy change in chemical reactions is heat change, and thus the major part of this sub-unit will be concerned with the heat changes that accompany chemical reactions.

cards.title: 5.1.3 Bond Breaking and Bond Formation
body: Chemical reactions usually involve the making or breaking of chemical bonds.
The energy of the product molecules may therefore be greater or less than the energy of the reactant molecules.

cards.title: 5.1.6 Energy-Level Diagrams
body: Energy is supplied to the reactants to raise the particles up to the higher energy level.

cards.title: 5.1.9 Thermochemical Equations
body: An equation that contains the information about the heat changes involved in a reaction is called a thermochemical equation.
The physical states of reactants and products should be stated.
The value of 'H given as kJ/mol refers to kJ per 1 mole of reactant or product as written in the equation:- i.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What happens thermodynamically when any chemical bond is broken inside a molecule?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define bond breaking energetics**
To break a chemical bond, attractive electrostatic forces between atoms must be physically overcome.

**Step 2: Identify energy direction**
Overcoming these forces requires an input of energy from the surroundings. Thus, bond breaking is always **endothermic** (absorbs energy).

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The correct choice is **Energy must be absorbed (endothermic).**

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In an energy-level diagram for an exothermic reaction, which of the following is true regarding the positions of the reactants and products?

options.A: Reactants are at a lower energy level than products.
options.B: Reactants and products are at the identical energy level.
options.C: Reactants are at a higher energy level than products.
options.D: The enthalpy change ($$\Delta H$$) is positive.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze exothermic thermodynamics**
In an exothermic reaction, heat is released because the reactants possess more total chemical potential energy than the products ($$H_{\text{reactants}} > H_{\text{products}}$$).

**Step 2: Relate to the energy diagram**
Therefore, on the vertical y-axis (Enthalpy/Energy), the reactants are positioned **higher** than the products.

**Step 3: Final Answer**
The correct statement is **Reactants are at a higher energy level than products.**

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In the hypothetical reaction: $$ X_2 + Y_2 \rightarrow 2XY + \text{Heat} $$

options.A: $$ \Delta H $$ is positive and the reaction is endothermic.
options.B: $$ \Delta H $$ is positive and the reaction is exothermic.
options.C: $$ \Delta H $$ is negative and the reaction is endothermic.
options.D: $$ \Delta H $$ is negative and the reaction is exothermic.
options.E: $$ \Delta H $$ may be positive or negative.

cards.why: When '+ Heat' is written on the product side of an equation, it means heat is being **released**. This defines an **exothermic** reaction. In exothermic reactions, the change in enthalpy (**$$ \Delta H $$**) is always **negative**.

lessons.title: Types of Heat of Reaction and Heat Changes

cards.title: Types of Heat of Reaction and Heat Changes
body: Main types: heat of combustion, solution, neutralisation, formation, fusion, vaporisation. Thermochemical equation prints ΔH next to the balanced reaction. Units: kJ / kJ mol⁻¹.

cards.title: Exo I exit heat. Endo I enter heat.
body: The flask of an exo reaction feels hot. Endo feels cold. Photosynthesis stores; combustion spends.

cards.title: Drawing and using energy diagrams
body: Sketch two horizontal lines (reactants, products) and a hump (Ea). If products sit lower, shade ΔH downward and write “exo, ΔH < 0”. If products sit higher, ΔH upward, endo. A catalyst cuts the hump, not the gap between the two lines.

Heat of combustion is usually quoted per mole of fuel burnt completely to CO₂ and H₂O. Heat of neutralisation for strong acid + strong base is about the same number every time because the reaction is really H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. Heat of formation is ΔH when 1 mol of compound is made from elements in their standard states.

When you compare fuels, divide heat released by mass (or by price) — a bigger mole ΔH is not automatically the better cooking fuel if the molecule is huge. Always check the state symbols: extra energy is hidden if a product is steam rather than liquid water.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The stored chemical energy inside a covalent molecular substance, which exists within the chemical bonds holding its atoms together, is classified as what kind of energy?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define energy types**
*   Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
*   Potential energy is stored energy due to position, composition, or chemical bonds.

**Step 2: Conclusion**
Chemical energy stored within the molecular bonds of a substance is a form of **potential energy**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following constant relationships is correct for converting heat energy units from calories to Joules?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall unit conversion factors**
By standard chemical definition:
$$1\text{ calorie (cal)} = 4.184\text{ Joules (J)} \approx 4.2\text{ Joules (J)}$$

**Step 2: Final Answer**
The correct relationship is **$$1\text{ calorie} = 4.2\text{ Joules}$$**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The stored energy contained in a substance is called
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define the types of energy.**
- Kinetic energy is energy of motion.
- Thermal energy is related to temperature.
- **Chemical energy** is the potential energy stored in the chemical bonds of a substance.

**Result:** Stored energy in a substance is chemical energy.

cards.title: Exam question, solved
cards.problem: The energy produced due to the motion of the particles of a substance is an example of  A) solar energy.  B) kinetic energy.  C) mechanical energy.  D) potential energy.  E) thermal energy.

steps.text: **Step 1.** **Thermal energy** is the energy contained within a system that is responsible for its temperature.
**Step 2.** It arises from the internal **kinetic energy (motion)** of the atoms and molecules making up the substance.

glossary.meaning: Heat of neutralization is the heat released when 1 mol of water is formed during the neutralization of an acid by an alkali.
The heat generated is called heat of hydration.
Energy is a property of matter that allows work to be done.
Temperature is the measure of the hotness or coldness of an object.

tips.text: Energy is a property of matter that allows work to be done.
Temperature is the measure of the hotness or coldness of an object.
The breaking of bonds requires or absorbs energy;the formation of bonds releases energy.
The average energy required to break a chemical bond is called the bond energy. Some salts dissolve endothermically; they require an input of energy for dissolving.
The quantity of heat absorbed or released during a chemical reaction can be shown in a chemical equation. There are different types of heat of reaction.
They involve various amounts of heat change, depending on the heat content of the products and the reactants.
Heat of neutralization is the heat released when 1 mol of water is formed during the neutralization of an acid by an alkali.
There are different types of heat of reaction and heat change, namely heat of combustion, heat of solution, heat of neutralization, heat of formation, heat of fusion and heat of vaporization.
The heat of neutralization of a strong acid and a strong base is the same - 57.1 kj/mol.

questions.answer: Heat given out to the surroundings. ΔH negative.
why: In an exothermic reaction energy is released to the surroundings, which get warmer; the products have less energy than the reactants, so ΔH is negative.

similar.q: All are correct about an exothermic reaction, except  A) ΔH is negative.  B) the products have less heat energy than the reactants.  C) heat is given off to the environment.  D) energy of the vessel becomes cooler because energy is released.  E) None of the above.
similar.a: D. energy of the vessel becomes cooler because energy is released. — Because heat is released, the vessel and its surroundings become WARMER, not cooler. D is false. Answer: D.

why: In an endothermic reaction energy is absorbed from the surroundings, which get colder; the products have more energy than the reactants, so ΔH is positive.
questions.label: 2. Endothermic means?

C) ΔH is negative and the reaction is endothermic.  D) ΔH is negative and the reaction is exothermic.  E) ΔH may be positive or negative.
similar.a: D. ΔH is negative and the reaction is exothermic. — The products have less enthalpy than the reactants, so ΔH is negative. Answer: D.

similar.a: D. heat of the reactants is greater than that of the products. — The released heat is the difference H(reactants) − H(products); therefore the reactants have more heat content than the products (ΔH < 0). Answer: D.

questions.q: Thermal decomposition of carbonate is often?
why: Breaking down a carbonate (e.g. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂) needs continuous heating — energy is taken in, so it is endothermic.

similar.q: The most common form of energy transformation in chemical reactions is in the form of  A) light energy.  B) solar energy.  C) heat energy.  D) chemical energy.  E) electrical energy.
similar.a: C. heat energy. — Chemical reactions may release or absorb light, electrical or heat energy, but by far the most common form of energy change is heat (exothermic and endothermic reactions). Answer: C.

C) enthalpy change when 1 mol of a substance is dissolved in water.  D) heat released when 1 mol of water is formed.  E) heat absorbed when 1 mol of water is formed.
similar.a: C. enthalpy change when 1 mol of a substance is dissolved in water. — B = heat of combustion; D = heat of neutralisation. Answer: C.

questions.answer: Heat released when 1 mol burns completely in oxygen.

questions.answer: Some ammonium / potassium salts going into water feel cold.

similar.q: An iron nail at a temperature of 80 °C is immersed into water at a temperature of 60 °C. Which statement is correct about the process?  A) The iron nail releases heat and the water absorbs.  B) The iron nail absorbs heat and the water releases.  C) Heat of 20 °C is transferred to the water.  D) The temperature of the water will be 140 °C.  E) A and D.
similar.a: A. The iron nail releases heat and the water absorbs. — Heat is measured in joules, not °C (C is wrong), and temperatures do not add (D is wrong). Answer: A.

questions.q: On an exo diagram products sit?
why: In an exothermic reaction energy is released, so the products have less energy and are drawn lower than the reactants on the energy diagram.

similar.q: The enthalpy change of a chemical reaction can be found from the  A) boiling and melting point difference of products and reactants.  B) solubility difference of products and reactants.  C) heat content difference of products and reactants.  D) electrons lost and gained during a reaction.  E) All of the above.
similar.a: C. heat content difference of products and reactants. — Enthalpy (H) is the heat content of a substance. The enthalpy change is ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants). Answer: C.

questions.q: Why a match is needed for methane + O₂?
questions.answer: To supply Ea even though the reaction is exo overall.
why: Even exothermic reactions need activation energy (Ea) to start breaking bonds; the match supplies this, then the heat released keeps the reaction going.
